stem:
Yash looks at the diagram of $\angle PQR$. He will measure $\theta$ with a protractor.

Which claim correctly states how he must place the protractor?

options.text: Put the protractor center on vertex $Q$, align ray $QP$ with the zero-degree line, and read the scale reached by ray $QR$.
Rest the protractor anywhere on ray $QP$ and read a scale mark for $\theta$.
Say that reading a degree number is what creates $\angle PQR$ on the page.
After reading $\theta$, treat that same reading as also fixing every unmarked angle at $Q$.

teacher.key_rationale: Measuring angle PQR needs the protractor center on Q, one arm on the zero line, and the other arm read on the same scale. Resting anywhere on a ray, reversing reading as what creates the angle, or extending one reading to every angle at Q all miss that placement.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as angle PQR with marked theta and a note that the protractor center goes on Q.
